title: Large steps first, small steps after: worlds that died, played on from iteration 500 with small mutations

thesis.claim: A world that starts with the engine's large mutations and goes on with small ones lives, where the same world left with the large ones dies. Played on from iteration 500 with mutations of 10 numbers, the three worlds of s3058 at 10,000 tokens that died out in Experiment 46 live 5,000 iterations more and become worlds of equals.
thesis.why: From founders, mutations of 10 numbers killed four of five worlds within 71 to 1,322 iterations (Experiment 56): founders' brains are drawn at random, and small steps are too slow to make them fit before the world breaks. The engine's mutation finds brains that live, but cannot keep a way of playing that needs everyone to follow it (Experiment 53). The world of equals so far formed twice from a world that had first run with large mutations, and once from founders. So large steps to begin with and small steps after should give both: a world that gets through its start, and then keeps its order. Under the engine's mutation these three worlds died at 744, 1,029 and 2,630 iterations.
thesis.confirm: A run is a world of equals if, over its last 500 iterations, there are fewer than 0.01 births per agent and iteration and at least nine nodes in ten are won by a coalition. Both: at least five of the six runs played on with 10 numbers live to iteration 5,500, and at least four of them are worlds of equals; and at most two of the six runs played on as they are live to 5,500.
thesis.refute: Fewer than three of the six runs with 10 numbers live to iteration 5,500, or as many runs live as they are as with 10 numbers. Anything else is undecided.
